messages:
marta: Quick question — for traces/metrics/logs, do we split pipelines per-signal at the agent or let the gateway fan out? I can see pros/cons but want to align before the design doc.
ashwin: My 2c: split as early as possible to cut downstream bandwidth. Agent-side <sampling/filtering> helps.
noah: Agree on bandwidth, but agent CPU on edge devices is limited. Some customers run agents on tiny instances.
ginger: We should consider exporter fan-out too. If gateway does fan-out we centralize auth/credentials for exporters.
olivia: Also retention paths differ — traces -> 30d, metrics -> 90d. Gateway-level routing makes TTL/retention enforcement easier.
ashwin: True. But if gateway enforces retention we still need per-tenant tagging from agent. Can't rely on gateway to invent tenant ids.
marta: Good point. Agents must preserve tenant metadata and context propagation. What about chaining exporters? e.g., gateway sends to internal buffer then to external A/B exporters.
infra-bot: Deploy checklist: ensure gateway has retry/backoff and backpressure to avoid OOM on fan-out.
ashwin: Can we do hybrid? Basic per-signal filtering at agent (only drop noisy spans/metrics), then gateway does heavy fan-out and enrichment + retention policy enforcement.
noah: Hybrid seems pragmatic. Also add a config flag: `agent.pipeline.split_signals: true|false` so enterprise can toggle.
ginger: UX note: console needs to show per-route metrics (eg. bytes in/out per signal) and allow per-route quotas. Otherwise ops will be blind.
marta: Draft plan: - agent tags and light filters, - gateway does fan-out/enrichment/retention, - export adapters one-per-destination with shared pool + circuit breaker. I'll sketch PR and config example.
olivia: Please include sample config in PR, e.g.
```
agent:
  pipeline:
    split_signals: true
    drop_rules:
      spans: [{probability: 0.5, match: "healthcheck"}]
gateway:
  exporters:
    - name: prod-apm
      type: otlp
    - name: longterm-archive
      type: s3
```
marta: Thanks — I'll open a PR and add pros/cons matrix. Tagging @ashwin and @ginger for review :thumbsup:
